- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) and price is trending down, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 2% from prior peak), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or apply mean reversion to prior 5-day average.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 10-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates final 5–7 days; apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to last 5–7 forecasted values.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.20 to -0.20), model lags in adjusting; apply 1–2 day lag correction to forecasted values.
